summary:
Keep a stack of days still waiting for a warmer one. Their temperatures never rise from bottom to top, because
a warmer day would have settled the cooler days below it. Each new day pops every waiting day that's cooler
and records the gap. Every day is pushed and popped once: O(n).

question.md:
For every day, how many days until a strictly warmer one? If none comes, 0.

- **Strictly warmer:** an equal temperature doesn't count.
- **The last day always gets 0.**
- **Up to 10⁵ days**; temperatures are between −100 and 100.

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Strictly warmer: an equal temperature doesn't end the wait.
- Days never followed by a warmer one keep 0.
- Temperatures range only over −100 … 100, which a value-indexed approach can use.

think.md:
**The monotonic stack idea.** Keep a stack of items that are still **waiting for an answer** (for example "the next
warmer day"). When a new item arrives, it answers every waiting item it beats; those are popped. Because each popped
item was beaten by the new one, the items left on the stack are always in sorted order (that's the "monotonic" part),
so the new item only needs to look at the top.

**Why it's O(n).** Every item is pushed once and popped at most once, so all the `while` loops together do at most
`n` pops, even though a single step may pop many.

**Waiting days.** The stack holds days still waiting for something warmer; their temperatures never increase from
bottom to top (a warmer day would have settled the ones before it). When a new day is warmer than the top, it is
the first warmer day for that top day: record the wait and pop, repeatedly. For `[30, 28, 31, 27, 27, 29, 33, 26]`:

approaches.title: Look ahead from every day

idea.md: From each day, scan forward to the first warmer day.

build: Record the distance to the first warmer day.

lines.text: Look ahead one day at a time.
The first strictly warmer day ends the wait.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²)** (e.g. decreasing temperatures). **Space O(1)** besides the output.

steps.text: Day 0 (30°): first warmer day is 2 (31°), wait 2.
Day 1 (28°): first warmer day is 2 (31°), wait 1.
Day 2 (31°): first warmer day is 6 (33°), wait 4.
Day 3 (27°): first warmer day is 5 (29°), wait 2.
Day 4 (27°): first warmer day is 5 (29°), wait 1.
Day 5 (29°): first warmer day is 6 (33°), wait 1.
Day 6 (33°): no warmer day ahead, wait 0.
Day 7 (26°): no warmer day ahead, wait 0.

walk.title: For each day, look forward day by day until a strictly warmer one.

limits.md: Scans the same stretch from many days. A stack answers each day exactly once, when its warmer day arrives.

approaches.title: Nearest later day for each temperature

idea.md:
Walk from the back, remembering for each temperature the nearest later day with it (`nxt[t]`). A day's
answer is the smallest `nxt[t']` over all warmer temperatures `t'`, which is at most 200 values to check.

build: From the back, take the nearest warmer day.

lines.text: `next[t + 100]` = nearest later day with temperature `t`; `n` stands for 'never'.
From the last day to the first, so `next` always describes the days after `i`.
Every strictly warmer temperature (index `temps[i] + 101` and up); the nearest such day is the first warmer day.
Found one: the wait is the gap.
Day `i` is now the nearest day with its temperature for everything before it.

steps.text: Day 7 (26°): remembered warmer temperatures {} (temp: day). None: wait 0. Now day 7 is the nearest 26°.
Day 6 (33°): remembered warmer temperatures {} (temp: day). None: wait 0. Now day 6 is the nearest 33°.
Day 5 (29°): remembered warmer temperatures {33: 6} (temp: day). Nearest is day 6: wait 1. Now day 5 is the nearest 29°.
Day 4 (27°): remembered warmer temperatures {29: 5, 33: 6} (temp: day). Nearest is day 5: wait 1. Now day 4 is the nearest 27°.
Day 3 (27°): remembered warmer temperatures {29: 5, 33: 6} (temp: day). Nearest is day 5: wait 2. Now day 3 is the nearest 27°.
Day 2 (31°): remembered warmer temperatures {33: 6} (temp: day). Nearest is day 6: wait 4. Now day 2 is the nearest 31°.
Day 1 (28°): remembered warmer temperatures {29: 5, 31: 2, 33: 6} (temp: day). Nearest is day 2: wait 1. Now day 1 is the nearest 28°.
Day 0 (30°): remembered warmer temperatures {31: 2, 33: 6} (temp: day). Nearest is day 2: wait 2. Now day 0 is the nearest 30°.

walk.title: Go backwards, remembering for every temperature the nearest later day that had it. A day's answer is the nearest of the remembered days that are warmer.

limits.md: Depends on the small temperature range; with arbitrary values it fails. The stack works for any values in O(n).

approaches.title: Stack of waiting days

idea.md:
Scan forward with a stack of waiting days. Each new day pops every waiting day that is colder, setting its
wait, then joins the stack.

**Invariant.** Temperatures on the stack are non-increasing from bottom to top, and every day still on the
stack hasn't seen a warmer day yet.

build: Pop colder days and set their waits.

lines.text: Waits default to 0; the stack holds days still waiting.
Day `i` is the first warmer day for every cooler day on top of the stack. Settle them; stop at a day at least as warm, since everything below it is warmer still.
Day `i` now waits for its own warmer day.

steps.text: Day 0 (30°): settles nobody. It starts waiting.
Day 1 (28°): settles nobody. It starts waiting.
Day 2 (31°): warmer than waiting days [1, 0]: their waits are [1, 2]. It starts waiting.
Day 3 (27°): settles nobody. It starts waiting.
Day 4 (27°): settles nobody. It starts waiting.
Day 5 (29°): warmer than waiting days [4, 3]: their waits are [1, 2]. It starts waiting.
Day 6 (33°): warmer than waiting days [5, 2]: their waits are [1, 4]. It starts waiting.
Day 7 (26°): settles nobody. It starts waiting.
Days [6, 7] never found a warmer day: their wait stays 0. Waits: [2, 1, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0].

walk.title: A stack of days still waiting for a warmer day; their temperatures never increase from bottom to top. Each new day settles every waiting day it's warmer than.

takeaways.md:
- **Next greater element:** stack of waiting indices; a new value settles all smaller ones on top.
- Store **indices**, so distances can be computed.
- **Pitfall:** `≤` instead of `<` (equal temperatures aren't warmer).
